text.p: Mexican telephone firm Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) is expected to report lacklustre 1996 results on an operating basis due to an economy that is finding it hard to shine after the 1994-1995 peso crisis, analysts said.

The average forecast of five industry analysts surveyed by Reuters predicted 1996 earnings would be $3.57 per ADR, using a year-end number of outstanding shares of 8.875 billion. That compares to 1995 net earnings per ADR of about $2.50.

Telmex's bottom line for the year as a whole is seen growing about 13 percent in real terms, but most of the gains are non-cash items due to fewer foreign exchange losses and monetary gains, analysts said.

On an operating level, the company is expected to show slight real gains of between 3-4 percent on 1995 results thanks to higher prices for local service and a small rebound in domestic long-distance traffic.
Analysts said that amortization charge will hurt operating profits, but will have a negligible impact on cash flow.
And because the charge is not deductible, the firm's tax bill may rise compared to previous quarters, analysts said.

In the fourth quarter alone, Telmex may show a slight recovery in line growth from the third quarter, when lines installed actually fell for the first time by about 18,000. But the quarter itself could still be disappointing, analysts warned.
"There will be net new lines, but it won't be anything to write home about," said Ricardo Peon, the director of analysis at Deutche Morgan Grenfell in Mexico City.

"I don't think we'll see any significant recovery in demand, because we haven't seen any recovery on the consumption side," said Leslie Marcus, a telecommunications analyst at Santander Investments in New York.

One silver lining in an otherwise dark report could be new reporting methods by the phone company that will give analysts a better insight into the profitability of its local versus long-distance service.
Because the company now faces long-distance competition, analysts said they could be pleasantly surprised at the profitability of local service.
